linear.text: Claim under test: Charge is compensated by both V (V3+ to V4+ to V5+) and Fe (Fe2+ to Fe3+) valence changes
Read the panel: F3d [XAS]
Ruling: At zero charge Fe edge sits ~2/3 toward the Fe3+ line; shift only ~1.6 of ~5.9 eV span; V between V3+ and V5+

traces.question: The claim under test is that charge is compensated by both V (V3+ to V4+ to V5+) and Fe (Fe2+ to Fe3+) valence changes. What does Figure 3d actually show about this compensation?
traces.answer_key: The panel qualifies the claim rather than fully bearing it out. At zero charge the Fe edge sits only about 2/3 of the way toward the Fe3+ line, and the edge shift is just ~1.6 eV of the ~5.9 eV span that a full Fe2+ to Fe3+ change would require, so Fe's redox contribution is partial rather than complete. The V edge sits between V3+ and V5+, consistent with the V side of the claim.
traces.grading: Answer key: the audit ruling on the panel, i.e. node o19.
